back: An organism whose cell lacks a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; DNA is free in the cytoplasm.

front: Typical size of a bacterium and of a virus?
back: Bacterium about 1–5 µm; virus about 20–300 nm.
Bacteria: circular, no histones, in the cytoplasm, plus plasmids. Eukaryotes: linear chromosomes with histones in a nucleus.
A small circle of DNA separate from the main chromosome, often carrying genes such as antibiotic resistance.
DNA or RNA core, protein capsid; some have an envelope from the host membrane. No ribosomes or cytoplasm.

front: Why do antibiotics not work on viruses?
back: Viruses lack the bacterial targets (peptidoglycan wall, 70S ribosomes, metabolism).

front: One argument that viruses are alive and one that they are not?
back: Alive: they have genes and reproduce and evolve inside hosts. Not alive: not cells, no metabolism, inert outside a host.
